rationale: Luke tells the same parable, the same private question, a short form of the Isaiah 6:9-10 words, and the same four-part explanation, in the same order as Matthew. Checked in this app’s BSB, the opening line is identical (“A farmer went out to sow his seed,” Matthew 13:3; Luke 8:5), and both Gospels have “the mysteries of the kingdom” in the plural (Matthew 13:11; Luke 8:10). The differences are checkable: Luke gives only “a hundredfold” (8:8); Luke’s Isaiah words are introduced with “so that” (8:10, Greek hina) and do not include the healing clause; Luke says the rocky-ground hearers “believe for a season” (8:13), names “the devil” (8:12) and adds “so that they may not believe and be saved” (8:12); and Luke’s good soil is “those with a noble and good heart, who hear the word, cling to it, and by persevering produce a crop” (8:15). Luke has no 13:16-17 at this point; a close form of that saying stands at Luke 10:23-24 (its own row). Graded parallel/strong on the same precedent as conn-matt13-sower-mark4 and conn-matt9-ruler-luke8.
